title: Choose the homepage composition
question: The identity, palette, content structure, and minimal-border rule are fixed. Which hierarchy should the implementation follow?

options.label: Balanced Split
options.lineage: the selected direction, refined to the approved green palette
options.thesis: The people growing the vegetables and the box being sold share the first viewport equally.
options.viewport: A large human greenhouse panel sits beside an equally strong featured-box purchase panel, with highlighted articles beginning at the fold.
options.risk: Two equal focal areas require careful spacing so the page still has one clear reading order.

options.label: Product Spotlight
options.lineage: the same identity with the featured box as the dominant weekly choice
options.thesis: One featured box becomes the unmistakable purchase decision without losing the greenhouse proof behind it.
options.viewport: The greenhouse fills the opening while one large pale-green product module overlaps the edge and keeps every buying detail visible.
options.risk: The product panel can feel detached if its overlap is too heavy or too card-like.

options.label: Greenhouse Ribbon
options.lineage: the same identity with the human greenhouse story leading
options.thesis: A continuous greenhouse scene earns trust first, then hands the eye directly to the featured box action.
options.viewport: A broad greenhouse ribbon occupies two-thirds of the screen while a compact vertical product stack contains the headline and purchase action.
options.risk: The right-hand stack needs responsive care so the headline and product controls never feel compressed.
